# A positive ordinary cap-ceiling band for the exact Lorentz rows

The new conclusion here is the exact inequality Phi_i<=2 for arbitrary
convex bodies in a cap-ceiling band. Ordinary inverse weights approaching
1/3 would follow from compactness alone and are not being claimed as a
new mechanism. The width of the band is proved positive but not computed;
in particular no comparison to128/279 or to the mixed ratio1/32 is made.

## 1. Statement and affine invariance

Let Gamma=4/9. There exists epsilon_0>0 with the following property.
Let K be any planar convex body, y in int K, and let v_1,v_2,v_3 be
spanning nonzero normals with v_1+v_2+v_3=0. Define the actual cap fractions
q_i, normalized sections sigma_i, and generalized row data by

    Q_i=|K intersect{v_i.(x-y)>=0}|,  q_i=Q_i/|K|,
    sigma_i=H_1(K intersect{v_i.(x-y)=0})/||v_i||,
    M=sum_i Q_i/sigma_i,
    f_i=2sqrt(|K| Q_i)/(sigma_i M),
    Phi_i=f_i+(f_j+f_l)^2/4.

If every q_i<=Gamma+epsilon_0, then all Phi_i<=2. If K is not a
triangle, all three inequalities are strict.

Under x'=L(x-y), transform every normal to L^(-T)v_i. All areas acquire
|det L|, and each coarea-normalized section sigma_i acquires the SAME
factor |det L|. This last identity follows from the planar tangent/normal
identity, or one-dimensional change of variables on the cutting line.
Hence M is unchanged and every f_i and Phi_i is unchanged. A common
positive rescaling of all normals divides every sigma_i by that scale
and multiplies M by it, also preserving all f_i. Independent rescalings
are not asserted to preserve the row data.

The main input is the fully proved ordinary theorem in
`candidate fed8703fd24ac57f`: every
fixed strict-incidence triangle has a full Hausdorff neighborhood, for
its fixed source and balanced normals, in which the Lorentz inequalities
hold, strictly for nontriangles. Its exact replacement, convergence,
roof estimates and strictness have independent root and Slab audits.

## 2. Complete compactness and equality argument

Suppose the stated band did not exist. For each m choose an offending
configuration with max_i q_i<=Gamma+1/m: either a row exceeds2, or a
nontriangular body has a row at least2. Each source is an actual interior
point and all sections are positive.

Choose a maximum-area inscribed triangle in each body and map its three
vertices to the fixed triangle T_ref=conv{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)}. Such a
maximum exists by continuity of the area on the compact triple product;
it has positive area because the body has interior. This affine map is
invertible and the row data are preserved as explained in Section1.
For every point x in the normalized body, replacing vertex i of T_ref
by x gives an inscribed triangle of area |lambda_i(x)|/2, where lambda_i
are the barycentric affine functions of T_ref. Maximality forces
|lambda_i(x)|<=1. Therefore all normalized bodies lie in one fixed
compact triangle Q and contain T_ref. Their maximal inscribed-triangle
areas remain exactly1/2.

Their support functions are uniformly bounded and Lipschitz on the unit
circle. A subsequence converges uniformly by Arzela--Ascoli, hence the
bodies converge in Hausdorff distance to a convex body K_* containing
T_ref and contained in Q. Vertexwise approximation shows that its
maximal inscribed-triangle area is at most1/2. The sources have a
convergent subsequence y_m to y_* in K_*.

Normalize the transformed normals individually to unit vectors u_i^m,
keeping their numerical balance weights

    a_i^m=||v_i^m||/sum_j ||v_j^m||,
    sum_i a_i^m u_i^m=0,    sum_i a_i^m=1.

The normals and weights have convergent subsequences. All three limiting
unit vectors remain nonzero. Cap areas converge: the body indicators
converge away from the null boundary of K_*, the moving halfplane
indicators converge away from their limiting lines, and all are bounded
in one fixed set. Dominated convergence applies, with body areas bounded
below by1/2. Thus each limiting cap has fraction at mostGamma.

No balance weight can vanish in the limit. A single remaining positive
weight cannot balance a nonzero unit vector. If exactly two remain,
their unit vectors must be opposite, with equal weights; their two
closed halfplanes through y_* are complementary and their fractions
sum to1, contradicting2Gamma<1. The limiting vectors also span the
plane: if they were collinear, positive balance would again supply an
opposite pair and the same contradiction. Hence the limit is a full
positive circuit; in particular any pair is linearly independent.

Let g_* be the ordinary centroid of K_*. Classical Grunbaum gives
fraction at leastGamma for any halfplane containing g_*. If one limiting
cap contained g_* strictly, its inward parallel translate through g_*
would still have fraction at leastGamma, and the removed strip would
have positive area because g_* is interior. Its original fraction would
then be greater thanGamma, a contradiction. Consequently

    u_i.(g_*-y_*)<=0 for every i.

The positive balanced sum of these three numbers is zero. They must
therefore all vanish, and spanning gives y_*=g_*. Every limiting cap now
contains the centroid, so every fraction equalsGamma.

The classical single-cap equality case of planar Grunbaum says that a
convex body attaining4/9 at its centroid is a triangle and the attaining
cap isolates one vertex with boundary parallel to the opposite edge.
Thus K_* is a triangle. It contains T_ref and its area is at most1/2 by
the maximal-triangle condition, so K_*=T_ref. The three equality caps
isolate its three different vertices strictly: two repeated equality
directions would force the third unit vector to be opposite by balance,
contradicting the complementary-area calculation above.

It remains to use the fixed-normal local theorem correctly despite the
moving normals. Put w_i^m=a_i^m u_i^m. These are the original balanced
normals rescaled by one COMMON positive factor. Let L_m be the matrix
whose rows are (w_1^m)^T and (w_2^m)^T. It is invertible for large m and
converges to an invertible L_*. Apply x'=L_m(x-y_m). The three transformed
normals are EXACTLY e_1,e_2,-e_1-e_2. Their bodies converge to the strict
centroid-cut triangle L_*(T_ref-g_*), with source fixed at zero. All row
data have been preserved by the two permitted operations. The proved
full local theorem now places every sufficiently late body inside its
valid neighborhood. It gives all rows at most2, strictly for every
nontriangle, contradicting the selected offending configurations.
This proves existence of epsilon_0>0 with the asserted exact conclusion.

Only classical Grunbaum and its single-cap equality characterization are
used as standard convex-geometric background in this argument. The
compact normalization and equality limit are also established in the
archived ordinary stability sources; the new exact conclusion uses the
full local Lorentz theorem, not continuity of Phi_i alone. At the limit
all f_i=1 and Phi_i=2, so continuity alone would not supply the required
inequality on either side of that boundary.

## 3. Relation to the attained ordinary stability modulus

The archived theorem
`candidate 40c46f71889ea6fc` supplies
an attained positive modulus for the ordinary surplus

    E=sum_i q_i-1-(3/4)min_i q_i>=0.

There is a useful explicit conversion from a cap ceiling to its premises.
If c=Gamma+epsilon bounds all q_i and m=min q_i, the cap-cover inequality
1<=(1/4)m+the other two fractions gives

    m>=4-8c=Gamma-8epsilon,
    0<=E<=(9/4)c-1=(9/4)epsilon.                      (1)

Thus epsilon<=1/36 ensures m>=2/9. For any specified stability tolerance
eta, taking additionally epsilon<=(4/9)epsilon_stab(2/9,eta) puts the
configuration in that theorem's simultaneously controlled body and cap
neighborhood. Continuous balanced-normal normalization then connects
it to the local Lorentz neighborhood, just as in Section2. This is an
alternative positive-modulus formulation; the values of those local
radii have not been evaluated here.

## 4. A scoped actual-fiber consequence

Suppose an actual planar three-fiber configuration has endpoint areas
a,b, middle area k, and a positive circuit of ambient caps through an
interior middle source. Assume each selected cap has zero area on the
B endpoint, common total area Q, and original-mass bound

    Q<=(Gamma/2)(a+k+b),      b<=a+k.

Its actual middle cap fractions satisfy, since the A contributions are
nonnegative,

    q_i<=Q/k<=Gamma(1+a/k).

Therefore a/k<=epsilon_0/Gamma places the ACTUAL middle body and source
in the exact Lorentz band. No replacement is applied to the mixed family;
the ordinary theorem is merely evaluated on its actual cap and section
data. This supplies the exact row inequalities in that sufficiently
small-endpoint regime, strictly if the middle body is not a triangle.

This does not assert a quantitative comparison to a/b<1/32, does not
turn ordinary section weights into mixed weights automatically, and
does not improve the archived nonquantitative small-endpoint center
repair by itself. Its distinct contribution is a proved exact ordinary
row inequality where the limiting triangle rows are equalities.
